## 2026-10-16 - 0.9.4.107 A/AB targeted enumeration implemented. Details: docs/build-history/0.9.4.107.en.md
### Problem
§7.3 measurements: A/AB verify only 0-1 pairs in the final pass yet analyze took 170.2-185.8 s — index 1.2-1.4 s + enumeration 168.8-184.4 s. With 0-64 changed files the pass still enumerated the whole dataset and discarded it via included() (candidate P-0.9.4.106-A-targeted-enum).
### Implementation
`consumeTargeted` in `ScanPipeline::analyze`: with `changedFiles`, each changed file queries the same indexes with its own hashes (images: full/mirror + normal crops only — same as `indexFile`; videos: +anchors). Discovered pairs dedup through the existing `seen`/`dedupCrop` set and run the **identical `process()`** (bestMatch -> verify/temporal -> included -> emission) — verdict parity. A/AB `candidates` now counts changed-touching pairs only (semantics documented). B unchanged.
### Verification
CPU 122/122, GPU 123/123, `--version` 0.9.4.107. `analyze_mode_test` 22 checks (+5: A/AB partial candidates=3, A cold == B, B unchanged). Field re-measurement pending (A/AB analyze expected in the 2-4 s class).
### Performance experiment index
P-0.9.4.107-A-targeted-enum — status PASS (implementation + field validation). Rationale: A/AB's fixed enumeration 168.8-184.4 s (§7.3, 0-64 changed) replaced by changed-count-proportional queries. Measured: user run `detailed-log-2026-10-16T041623.json` (mode A, 33 changed, 177,660 files) — analyze **1.9 s** (index 1.36 + **scan 0.19** + verify 0.33); the previous 168.8-184.4 s scan bucket is gone. Limits: AB cold (all changed) still queries every file (same class as before). Revisit: query cost at tens-of-thousands changes — changed-only temporary index or partition-scan hybrid.

## 2026-10-16 - 0.9.4.109 View-mode overlap recurrence fix (warm-cache icon re-apply). Details: docs/build-history/0.9.4.109.en.md
### Problem
User report: switching the view mode (List/Details/Tiles -> Extra Large/Large) makes images overlap each other or another view mode — a recurrence of the 0.9.4.66 overlap.
### Cause (vs the past fix)
The 0.9.4.66 fix's core was catch-up **replacing icons and forcing a layout pass**. The P3 async migration (0.9.4.69-.71) turned catch-up into a request pump that ignores `fileThumb()`'s return -> **cache-hit items get no request and no arrival, so they keep their old-size pixmap** -> a warm-cache XL->L->XL round trip recomputes only the cells, painting big art in small cells (overlap). The probe missed it because its catchup scenarios drop the cache first (all-miss path only).
### Implementation
`thumbCatchUpVisible`: cache hits are applied in place (`setIcon` via cacheKey compare) + coalesced layout; misses stay request-only (placeholder not applied). `groupViewChanged`: calls `thumbCatchUpVisible()` after the delegate/size swap. Test `ui_scroll` phase 21 (warm-cache round trip, hook `testCachedThumb`); a neutralized-fix probe reproduced `XL icon restored=0` FAIL before restoring the fix.
### Verification
CPU 122/122, GPU 123/123, `--version` 0.9.4.109. Phase 21 `XL=1 L=1` (checks=85). Field visual check (repeated round trips) needed.
### Performance experiment index
(Not a performance experiment — display bug fix. Zero added decodes.)
### Version
0.9.4.108 -> 0.9.4.109. engine/DB/schema/cache unchanged.

## 2026-10-16 - 0.9.4.110 Wheel-speed restore after view-mode switches (List latch fix). Details: docs/build-history/0.9.4.110.en.md
### Problem
User report: after visiting List/Details/Tiles and returning to an icon mode (XL/L/M/S), mouse-wheel scrolling becomes extremely slow — "it never returns to the icon-view wheel speed after the list view", persisting until an app restart.
### Cause (confirmed in the Qt 6.11 sources)
One wheel notch scrolls `singleStep() x wheelScrollLines(3)`. Qt item views push the mode step automatically while `viewMayChangeSingleStep` is set (icons = cell size + spacing, list = 1). But ListMode calls the **public** `setSingleStep(1)`, which **latches** `viewMayChangeSingleStep=false` (`QAbstractSlider::setSingleStep` re-enables it only for `step<0`). Every later automatic step update from the icon modes is ignored, so the step stays 1 (wheel = 3px). Measured (phase 22, pre-fix): `xl=175 list=1 back=1`.
### Implementation
`groupViewChanged`: right after the delegate/size swap, `verticalScrollBar()->setSingleStep(-1)` + `horizontalScrollBar()->setSingleStep(-1)` (re-enables the automatic step) -> the existing `doItemsLayout()` re-pushes the current mode's step via `updateGeometries()`. List mode's own behavior (item unit 1) is unchanged. Test `ui_scroll` phase 22 (XL->List->XL; pre-fix `back=1` FAIL reproduced, post-fix `back=175` PASS, checks=88).
### Verification
CPU 122/122, GPU 123/123, `--version` 0.9.4.110. Phase 22 `xl=175 list=1 back=175`. Field visual check (wheel speed after round trips) needed.
### Performance experiment index
(Not a performance experiment — input (wheel) behavior bug fix. Cost: two step resets, the layout pass is reused.)
### Version
0.9.4.109 -> 0.9.4.110. engine/DB/schema/cache unchanged.

## 2026-10-16 - 0.9.4.111 G4 IPC backpressure + G6 Job Object/GUI-exit verification (process-split release gates). Details: docs/build-history/0.9.4.111.en.md
### Problem
Active Build Queue priorities 2-3: G4 (send/flush blocking paths, bounded queue, slow-consumer lossless/coalescing/memory bound) and G6 (Win32 return handling, parent-death backend-PID E2E) sat at `OPENCODE REVIEW REQUIRED / not validated`. User instruction: start from priority 1 and continue.
### Cause (two real G6 defects confirmed)
(1) `shutdown()` polled `proc_->state()` to wait for exit — Qt processes `QWinEventNotifier`'s `WinEventAct` only during event-loop dispatch (qwineventnotifier.cpp:198), so the poll without an event loop could never observe the exit and burned the full `shutdownWaitMs` (3 s) on every app exit (measured 3049 ms). (2) `assignJobObject()` ignored the returns of `SetInformationJobObject`/`OpenProcess`/`AssignProcessToJobObject` with no logs (silent orphan-protection loss). G4: no defect confirmed (GUI->Backend bounded by the pending cap; Backend->GUI lossless with backlog = output size) — the missing evidence was added as a stress test.
### Implementation
`shutdown()`: `explicitShutdown_` guard (no double wait) + `proc_->disconnect(this)` (blocks the blocking drain's synchronous readyRead from re-entering GUI handlers) + `waitForFinished(shutdownWaitMs)` (direct handle wait) + `terminate()` only on timeout. `assignJobObject()`: all four Win32 calls return-checked with `GetLastError` logs, `PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS` -> `PROCESS_SET_QUOTA|PROCESS_TERMINATE|PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION`, test-only `jobObjectEnabled` option. `backend_main.cpp`: `MSF_TEST_BACKEND_WEDGE` seam (reader starts, event loop never entered -> SHUTDOWN and EOF self-exit both blocked). `backend_e2e_test` checks=37 (dataset 30->300 groups): Test 4 (G4 3 s consumer stall then drain: 0 gaps, 600 delivered, RSS 20/20/21 MB), Test 5 (G6 exit time: pre-fix 3049 ms FAIL reproduced -> post-fix 6 ms, PID gone), Test 6 (G6 parent-crash E2E: wedged backend reaped by the job, `--no-job` control survives -> job is load-bearing, explicit cleanup).
### Verification
CPU 122/122, GPU 123/123, `--version` 0.9.4.111. `backend_e2e_test` checks=37 (test5 pre-fix FAIL -> post-fix PASS). Full CPU CTest, no regressions.
### Performance experiment index
(Not a performance experiment — gate verification/lifecycle fix. Measured: exit 3049->6 ms; G4 stress RSS 20/20/21 MB, 600 matches lossless.)
### Version
0.9.4.110 -> 0.9.4.111. engine/DB/schema/cache unchanged.

## 2026-10-16 - 0.9.4.112 S4 GUI Detailed Logs save/exit acceptance (save unit split + real-button E2E). Details: docs/build-history/0.9.4.112.en.md
### Request/Trigger
User instruction: continue past priority 1 (G4/G6) to the next task. Queue priority 2 (S4): "final screen + save acceptance — verify the real Search/Update -> Detailed Logs -> save/exit path + reconcile the doc status conflict". The existing acceptance test covered generation/display/content only; save path, failure branch and exit were unverified.
### Cause (real defect)
The save was inlined in the dialog lambda (not unit-verifiable) and the write condition `write() >= 0` could report **a zero/partial write as "saved"**.
### Implementation
`MainWindow::saveDetailedLogTo(path,json)` split out (exact byte count, success/failure status message, bool return) + hook `testSaveDetailedLog`. Test extension: the real Save click runs via a **zero-delay singleShot** (Qt does not re-enter the same timer while its handler is on the stack, so the closer could not handle the file dialog opened by a click inside its own emission — measured), the picker's **name edit is set directly** (`selectFile` skips the name when the name edit has focus — measured), accept only once the dialog reports the target path, and the status is captured right after the save (same callstack; later scan-finish messages overwrite it — measured). Assertions: file exists, saved record == telemetry record (JSON equality), status shows the path, unwritable path fails (false), exit proceeds. S4 brief (ko/en) current-state updated (functional acceptance automated PASS; on-screen visual stays "not done" headless; final CLOSED tied to product acceptance).
### Verification
CPU 122/122, GPU 123/123, `--version` 0.9.4.112. `scan_detailed_log_acceptance_test` `save=ok`, `--repeat until-fail:3` 3 consecutive PASS (1.2-1.3 s). Full CPU CTest, no regressions.
### Performance experiment index
(Not a performance experiment — acceptance verification/save false-success fix.)
### Version
0.9.4.111 -> 0.9.4.112. engine/DB/schema/cache unchanged.

## 2026-10-16 - 0.9.4.113 Independent-audit items B1-B3, B7 (full-content badge + analyze-mode round trip + no-FFmpeg SKIP). Details: docs/build-history/0.9.4.113.en.md
### Request/Trigger
User instruction: continue in the audit report's priority order. Items: B1 (badge mislabel, FAIL reproduced), B2 (settings-to-record round-trip test gap), B3 (color_thumb no-FFmpeg R1), B7 (doc consistency).
### Cause/Findings
- B1: `sameContent` = size + 64 KiB quick hash (scanner.cpp:61) -> same size, same head, different tail was `identical=true` (audit probe reproduction). The quick-load path (media_search_engine.cpp:74-76) duplicated the rule.
- **Real defect found during verification (data race)**: the new memo was first an unsynchronized `unordered_map`; 16 final-pass shard threads inserted concurrently, corrupting the map and hanging `analyze()` (no `analyzeSlice`/`analyzeShards` lines; instrumentation changed timing and hid it — a Heisenbug found by the full suite as an e2e test4 180 s timeout).
### Implementation
- B1: the quick hash is a **candidate gate only**; passing pairs are confirmed by `sha256FileHex` (exposed in dataset_fingerprint.h, reusing the existing SHA-256) **full-content equality**. Per-file memo shared by the live/final passes (`std::mutex`, I/O outside the lock). Files above 512 MiB lose the badge (false negatives allowed, false positives not). `loadMatches` uses the same contract with a per-load memo. Measured cost (user index, read-only): 2,444 groups / 3,493 pairs / 5,296 files -> ~1.5 GiB extra reads per scan, 0 above the cap.
- B2: `backend_e2e_test` Test 1 `ui/analyzeMode=1` -> received telemetry `"mode":"A"`, Test 4 0 -> `"B"` (hook `testLastTelemetryJson`; checks 37->39). The `.107` cause stays unconfirmed until reproduced.

## 2026-10-17 - 0.9.4.114 Hotfix: Load / Start-Scan backend crash (loadMatches reference-invalidation UAF). Details: docs/build-history/0.9.4.114.en.md
### Problem
Field report (0.9.4.113, G:\Downloads\ss_twit): Load crashed the backend (exit code 62097) repeatedly with the "loading index" notice hanging; Start Search showed the same. The log confirmed `crash exit, code 62097`.
### Cause
The .113 B1 per-file hash memo in `loadMatches` **returned a reference into an unordered_map** — the second `fullHex` insert/rehash invalidated the first reference (`ha`) -> a dangling comparison (UAF) -> heap corruption/crash. Its callers (Load `backend_session.cpp:347`, scan quick-load `scan_worker.cpp:135`) match both symptoms exactly. Small CI datasets passed because the freed memory was not reused (latent).
### Implementation
`fullHex` now **returns by value (std::string)** and `ha`/`hb` are values, removing the lifetime problem. Regression test: a field-scale case in `search_engine_test` (3,000 noise BMP pairs / 6,000 files -> scan -> saveMatches -> loadMatches, asserting every pair's contentIdentical; `load_matches_big=ok pairs=3000`). The neutralized (reference-returning) version also passes synthetically — recorded that the UAF is nondeterministic and the field crash is the reproduction.
### Verification
CPU 122/122, GPU 123/123, `--version` 0.9.4.114. `search_engine_test` PASS (post-fix). The user's index DB is undamaged (SQLite crash safety; no writes during the load processing).
### Performance experiment index
(Not a performance experiment — hotfix. Load now reads candidate files once for the badge (~1.5 GiB) — check the feel.)
### Version
0.9.4.113 -> 0.9.4.114. engine/DB/schema/cache unchanged.

## 2026-10-17 - 0.9.4.115 Hotfix 2: the 62097 crash loop (event-thread block + stale kill timer). Details: docs/build-history/0.9.4.115.en.md
### Problem
The same 62097 crash persisted in .114 (field re-report). Log + Qt sources identified it: `KillProcessExitCode=0xf291` (62097) is the supervisor's `kill()` code (not a self-crash).
### Cause (two + one leftover)
- D1 (.113 regression): `BackendSession::loadIndex` runs synchronously on the IPC event thread; since .113 the badge confirmation reads candidate files (~1.5 GiB) -> 10 s+ silence -> health timeout (quiet 1/3 -> 3/3) -> terminate (ineffective on a console app) -> kill after 3 s (0xf291). Log: `health quiet 1/3` -> `watchdog: backend health timeout` -> `crash exit, code 62097`.
- D2 (pre-existing latent): `spawn()` never stopped `escTimer_` (only reset `escStage_` to 0) — the stale timer's stage-0 branch killed each fresh backend with no reason logged -> a self-sustaining kill loop. The .78 comment's intent was not enforced.
- Leftover: the Load row builder recomputed the badge from the quick hash only (the .113/.114 contract was not reflected).
### Implementation
D1: `loadIndex` -> QThread worker (`runLoadIndex`), `teardownWorker` -> `stopLoad()` serialization, seam `MSF_TEST_SLOW_LOAD_MS`. D2: `escTimer_.stop()` in `spawn()`. Leftover: rows use `m.contentIdentical`. Tests: Test 1b (12 s load survives — pre-fix FAIL reproduced), Test 3c (kill-reason invariant — pre-fix `reasonless=3` FAIL -> 0), checks 39->45.
### Verification
CPU 122/122, GPU 123/123, `--version` 0.9.4.115. e2e checks=45. The user's index DB is undamaged.
### Performance experiment index
(Not a performance experiment — hotfix. The one-time candidate read (~1.5 GiB) on Load / scan quick-load stays — revisit progress/cap if the feel is bad.)
### Version
0.9.4.114 -> 0.9.4.115. engine/DB/schema/cache unchanged.

## 2026-10-17 - 0.9.4.116 Phantom group members from external deletes fixed + GUI auto-repair. Details: docs/build-history/0.9.4.116.en.md
### Problem
Field report: group 275 (representative Keren1286444-2080011532100890711-01.jpg) — all similar files had been deleted yet the group stayed listed with two non-existent members (cached detail values but 0-byte size / blank resolution). Plus a request: auto-resolve such residuals in the GUI.
### Cause
The scan reconciliation used `Database::remove()` (**files row only**) -> `matches`/`thumbs` survived -> even a rescan never removed the pairs, so the phantom member persisted forever (no files row: size 0, blank detail). The monitor path (`removePath`, monitor.cpp:297) had the same defect. Load/quick-load displayed rows unvalidated.
### Implementation
Extracted `forgetRows` + added `forgetNoTransaction` (files+matches+thumbs inside the scan's outer transaction; `forget` keeps its own-transaction contract). `removePath` -> `db_.forget({path})`. **Auto-repair API `cleanupMissingOnDisk(root)`**: only when root is a directory; validates stored match endpoints -> forgets vanished paths + `diskCleanup missing=N` log (no-op on an offline root). **Runs automatically on Load (`runLoadIndex`) and scan quick-load before the list is built** -> the GUI auto-resolution. Tests: delete+rescan match removal (pre-fix exit 29 FAIL reproduced -> PASS), cleanup/offline no-op (30-33).
### Verification
CPU 122/122, GPU 123/123, `--version` 0.9.4.116. `search_engine_test` FAIL-first (29) -> PASS. `monitor_test` stays PASS. Field visual check needed (group 275 disappears + the `diskCleanup` log).
### Performance experiment index
(Not a performance experiment — cleanup/display fix. Cost: one existence stat per match endpoint on Load / scan start — a few hundred ms.)
### Version
0.9.4.115 -> 0.9.4.116. engine/DB/schema/cache unchanged.

## 2026-10-17 - 0.9.4.117 Bulk result-apply stall removed (deferred chunked fill + metadata request storm fix). Details: docs/build-history/0.9.4.117.en.md
### Problem
Field observation (.115 session): the GUI stalled for a long time when a Load completed (supervisor `health quiet 1/3` = 10 s+, minutes by later analysis). Adopted as "next-build candidate 1".
### Cause (three, measured by the probe)
(1) The tie sorting in `rebuildGroups` called `filePixels -> fileResolution`, which **issues a backend FILE_META request per path** on cache misses (with an ffprobe child-process fallback per path on the loopback) — 1,000 groups = 65.9 s (the dominant part of the 609.7 s synthetic 9,055-group synchronous apply). (2) `fillPair`'s synchronous bulk fill (two widget items per group). (3) `thumbCatchUpVisible` calling `visualItemRect` for every row.
### Implementation
(1) `filePixels` is cached-only (no requests/ffprobe; tie order degrades to size/path). (2) A `GroupFillJob` deferred fill above 800 rows (100 rows per event-loop turn, `fillGen_` generation cancels, per-chunk `setUpdatesEnabled`/`blockSignals` guards, anchor restore + catch-up + `groupFill done` log on completion; an append arriving mid-flight is demoted to a full rebuild). (3) Catch-up bounded to the visible window (`itemAt`-based +/-4 rows, full-range fallback). (4) Permanent `resultsApply`/`groupFill` stage logs. Regression probe `group_fill_perf_probe` (CTest `group_fill_probe`): a 9,055-group real-path apply checks return time, timer ticks and both pane row counts (pre-fix FAIL reproduced).
### Verification
CPU 123/123 (incl. the new probe), GPU 124/124, `--version` 0.9.4.117. Probe: 9,055 groups `applyMs=84 fillMs=18084 ticks=91` (pre-fix `applyMs=609,668 ticks=1`); 1,000 groups rebuild 65,856 ms -> 3 ms. Full regressions clean.
### Performance experiment index
P-0.9.4.117-group-fill — status **PASS**. Purpose: remove the GUI synchronous block in bulk result application. Baseline (pre-fix): 9,055-group synchronous apply 609,668 ms, ticks 1. Change: cached-only filePixels + deferred chunks (800/100) + catch-up window. Result: applyMs 84 ms, fill 18,084 ms asynchronous (91 ticks), 1,000-group rebuild 3 ms. Dataset: synthetic (probe, no disk access). Limit: the total fill time (9k ~ 18 s, ~2 ms/row = two widgets) remains — revisit conditions: lazy hidden-pane fill / model separation / persistent index.
### Version
0.9.4.116 -> 0.9.4.117. engine/DB/schema/cache unchanged.

## 0.9.4.118 — Scan list churn removed (append-first reuse + deferred large appends)

Field feedback (.117): Load progressive fill OK, thumbnails faster OK, group-275 resolution OK. The scan-time list was reported as "a few fast in the first scroll -> very slowly one-by-one -> then a big burst".
### Cause analysis (user session log, 05:03-05:16)
The same 9,057-row full rebuild repeated four times: right after Load 05:04:46 (16.2 s) / scan start 05:08:38 (20.5 s) / scan end 05:14:45 (19.0 s) / a later apply 05:16:23 (16.8 s). `beginScan` cleared the pane state (bestPct_/resCache_/pathKind_/thumbCache_ ...) and then called `refreshGroupList()` (append=false), re-creating every row and dropping the thumbnail cache even though the groups were unchanged. `onResults` / `scanFinished` / `scanFailed` did the same.
### Change
(1) `refreshGroupList(true)` on the four scan paths (prefix guard; identical list = no-op, a merge falls back to the automatic full rebuild). (2) Appends above 300 rows are deferred via `GroupFillJob(append)` (no pane clear, 100 rows/turn, `groupFill done ... append` log). (3) `group_fill_probe` gained Scenario A (repeat apply keeps the rows) and B (fresh-window first apply prompt).
### Verification
Two FAIL-first cycles: A `rowsKept=0` (pre-fix), B `applyMs=15,087/15,641 ms` (without append deferral) -> post-fix checks=8 PASS (repeat apply 101 ms rowsKept=1, fresh window 77 ms). CPU CTest 123/123, GPU CTest 124/124, `--version` 0.9.4.118. No regressions. Note: `view_mode_probe` failed twice under the post-build load and passed all four quiet runs of the same binary - recorded as a load-sensitive flake.
### Performance experiment index
P-0.9.4.118-scan-churn — status **PASS**. Purpose: remove the repeated rebuild (churn) of an unchanged list on the scan paths. Baseline (pre-fix): a repeat apply of an identical list re-created every row (user log: 16-20 s x4). Change: append-first on the four paths + deferred large appends (300). Result: repeat apply 101 ms keeping the rows (no-op level), fresh window 77 ms. Dataset: synthetic (probe, no disk access). Limit: the one-by-one streaming of genuinely new groups during a scan (engine pace) remains by design.
### Field confirmation (2026-10-17 06:40 session, build 0.9.4.118)
`detailed-log-2026-10-17T064028.json` cross-check: every summary line matches the JSON (AB/auto; wall 350.1 s = walk 303.7 + analyze 1.7; scanned 177,781 / analyzed 5 / unchanged 177,776; matches 1 pair / 1 group / 2 duplicate files; GPU 5/5, fallback 0; CPU avg 2.2% / mem 1018 MB; GPU duty 0.0% / longest idle 282.5 s). Incremental fingerprint reuse works (no 69.2 GB re-hash; process read 21.3 GB = two quick-hash passes). Display semantics recorded: the image throughput 39.8 files/s = analyzed/imageStage; the file line 0.0 files/s = analyzed/wall. The GUI churn absence needs the separate `msf_scan.log` check.

## 0.9.4.129 — Hybrid (AB) live-match loss fixed (live-index off-by-one)

Fixed the production code after reproducing and root-causing a field report (Auto/mixed-verification scans showed similar groups 0 and duplicate files 0; detailed log `pairs 0, reduction 100.0%`).
### Diagnosis path
- On an 18-file fresh index, only AB showed `pairs=0 liveBatches=0 verifyCalls=0 candidates=8` while Sequential showed `pairs=8` -- the AB final pass skips both-changed pairs (live-owned), and live delivered nothing.
- An isolated probe calling `ScanPipeline::addAndMatch` directly emitted successfully, so the pipeline itself was healthy. Tracing the production path showed `addAndMatch` emitting matches before `files_.push_back`, making the right index == `files_.size()`; the consumer `liveEmit` bounds check rejected every one of them. The live stream had delivered zero matches since 0.9.4.81.
### Change
- `addAndMatch`: collect matches, register the file (push + index), then emit -- same contract as batch analyze().
- Engine: fold AB live-owned image pairs into the report/telemetry (`nLiveImgPairs`, r.groups / r.imgPairs); a path-keyed union-find merges the live and final streams the same way the GUI does. `streamedMatches` is incremented for AB live only (no double counting in A/B).
- Limit live-pipe feeding to A/AB (Sequential is contracted to post-walk verification and its final pass emits every pair; prevents double emission into pending -- walker_queue_test pins the exact set).
- Search-summary CPU row now shows process (avg/max/std) plus the system mean (cpuSysMean) with two new keys. The reported "CPU 2%" was the process metric normalized by logical CPU count; the system mean existed only in the JSON and was never displayed.
### Verification
- Mode parity (18-file fresh index): B/A/AB all `pairs=8 groups=8 candidates=8`; telemetry all `pairs=8 candidates=8 imgGroups=3 imgDupFiles=8`. AB `verifyCalls=0` (final pass skipped = live ownership proven).
- Real JPEG cohort (xmp-med, 134 files) AB fresh index: `pairs=1 groups=1 imgGroups=1 imgDupFiles=2`.
- Regression pin: `walker_queue_test` case F (AB, 12 BMPs) -- `pairs=66, r.groups=66, imgGroups=1, imgDupFiles=12`; 0 before the fix.
- CPU CTest 125/125, GPU CTest 126/126.
### Version
0.9.4.128 -> 0.9.4.129. Verdicts/storage/protocol/engine/DB/schema/cache and journal schema unchanged. A mode's final-pass duplicate emission stays by design (GUI union-find absorbs it); B's observed behavior is unchanged.

## 0.9.4.130 — Match-set completeness baseline (A/AB self-heal)

After upgrading to 0.9.4.129 the field log (`detailed-log-2026-10-19T053207.json`) showed an AB scan with `analyzed 0, unchanged 177887, candidates 0, pairs 0, groups 0`. The file index was complete but the match store had never been populated (the 0.9.4.81-128 bug), and A/AB never recompute unchanged files -- they display the stored set -- so they cannot self-heal.
### Diagnosis path
- Reproduced on the 18-file set (store deleted + all unchanged + AB): pre-fix `pairs 0`, while a fresh Test Mode scan found `pairs 8` -- the engine is healthy; the production path merely recomputes nothing against an empty store.
- One Stable (B) scan heals it via the full pass (measured on 0.9.4.129: candidates=8 verifyCalls=8, store rebuilt), but upgrading users have no way to know that.
- The engine_version stamp cannot prove completeness (`revalidateMatches` writes it even for an empty set).
### Change
- New DB meta key `match_baseline`: the engine version under which a full-coverage verification last completed for the index.
- When it is missing for the current engine, A/AB run this one scan as a B-equivalent full pass (changedPtr=nullptr, live off, live-owned accounting off) and stamp it on completion. Cancelled/failed scans do not stamp and retry next scan. Backend log `matchBaseline=forceFullPass`.
- An engine-version bump invalidates the baseline automatically, so the next A/AB scan re-establishes it once. Zero file re-analysis.
### Verification
- Regression pin `walker_queue_test` case G: seed scan -> delete `matches` + `match_baseline` -> a Hybrid scan over unchanged files rediscovers 66 pairs and stamps the marker -> a follow-up scan recomputes nothing (pre-fix code fails with 0 pairs).
- Session probe: first AB scan with the baseline missing `candidates=8 verifyCalls=8`; after the stamp `candidates=0 verifyCalls=0 pairs=8` (quick-load). CPU CTest 125/125, GPU CTest 126/126.
### Version
0.9.4.129 -> 0.9.4.130. Verdicts/storage/protocol/engine/DB/schema/cache and journal schema unchanged. A/AB users pay one full verification on their first scan (usual speed afterwards). The counter-vs-quick-load numeric difference on unchanged rescans is a pre-existing display gap (separate candidate).

The panel even switched bases (groups_.size() during scans, lastStats_[3] pair count at finish).
### Change

## 0.9.4.133 — System CPU metric corrected + walk-phase CPU attribution measured

Field "CPU usage very different" (Maximum, nothing else running): log system avg 66.7% vs Task Manager 35-50% vs app process 1.7%.
### Root cause
- `sampleOnce` formula: `1 - idle/(idle+kernel+user)` -- GetSystemTimes kernel time includes idle, so idle was double-added in the denominator. Mathematically always reports `1/(2-u)` -> an idle machine reads >=50%.
- Measured (near-idle 5 s window, side by side): old formula 55.8% / corrected 20.6% / performance counter 17.1-23.8%. Field 66.7% -> true ~50%.
- `monitor.cpp` always used the correct formula -- the error was in the telemetry recorder only (swept).
### Change
- Header-inline `systemBusyPercent(dI,dK,dU) = (dK+dU-dI)/(dK+dU)`, empty=0 with clamp. `sampleOnce` calls it.
- `benchmark_test` gains five formula checks (empty/idle/busy/mixed/inverted). The pre-fix formula fails the mixed case (0.667 vs 0.409).
### Attribution measurement (walk-only, exact product Scanner path, G:\Downloads\ss_twit 177,887 files, no-change)
- App (probe_walk) avg 1.66% (of 16 cores), peak 2.9% -- matches the field log's 1.7% and Task Manager's 2% (the metric is accurate).
- **Windows Defender (MsMpEng) avg 31.0%** (peak 37.3%) -- real-time scan of every file open. System total 65.2% (idle baseline 20.1%).
- Conclusion: the real ~50% is outside the app (antivirus). Recommended: exclude the scan root in Defender. Follow-up candidate: skip the walk quick-hash when (size,modified) match (a no-change walk still reads 21.2 GB).
### Verification
- Concurrent probe telemetry 17.5% vs counter avg 15.4% (max 24.5). CPU CTest 125/125, GPU CTest 126/126.
### Historical correction (AGENTS 9)
- System avg values in logs/dialogs from 0.9.4.88-132 are inflated. Original records kept; error cause, corrected formula and reason recorded in build-history. 66.7% -> true ~50%.
### Version
0.9.4.132 -> 0.9.4.133. Verdicts/storage/protocol/engine/DB/schema/cache unchanged. JSON keys unchanged (value definition corrected).

## 0.9.4.134 — Fast-rescan setting + forced duplicate re-verification

Following the 0.9.4.133 measurement (a no-change rescan's 5 minutes are dominated by per-file open I/O; app CPU 1.66%, Defender 31%), the two approaches the user chose are implemented. The Test Mode difference report + Yes/No adoption moves to the next build.
### (1) Fast rescan (setting, default OFF = strict)
- `ScanControl.fastRescan` wired through ScanWorker/BackendScanConfig/START_SCAN payload/backend_main; detailed log records `config.fastRescan`.
- `Scanner::ScanCallbacks.skipQuickHash`: only files with a stored row, matching (size,mtime), and no pending re-analysis skip the 64 KiB hash read. Files to be analyzed (pendingAnalysis), stat mismatches and video regrids still hash (fresh rows keep the badge/fingerprint-cache inputs). One hash implementation via `Scanner::quickHash64k`.
- Change detection: fast mode drops the quick-hash term (an empty hash is never treated as a mismatch). Strict remains the default, so existing verdicts are unchanged; the tooltip states the residual risk.
### (2) Forced re-verification (toolbar "Re-verify", duplicate members only)
- `reverifyStoredDuplicates`: stats + 64 KiB hash of members only (no walk) -> re-analyze only the changed ones (images batched / videos single) -> re-verify/rediscover only pairs touching a change through the targeted pass (d=8); unrelated stored pairs keep their verdict.
- Atomicity: rows, pairs and the match set update in ONE transaction (new `saveMatchesNoTransaction`); cancel/failure rolls everything back.
- `REVERIFY_INDEX` IPC (additive) + Load-style UI/notice + `REVERIFY_FINISHED` counter status line.
### Verification
- walker_queue case I: after a preserved-mtime edit, fast `analyzed=0` vs strict `analyzed=1`.
- Case J: `members=6 checked=6 changed=1 reanalyzed=1 pairs 15->10`, persisted (loadMatches 10).
- backend_e2e Test 1c: re-verify click -> results+counters, no backend restart, summary keeps `300 / "- / 300"`. Eight ui_settings keys. CPU 125/125, GPU 126/126.
### Version
0.9.4.133 -> 0.9.4.134. Verdicts/storage/protocol/engine/DB/schema/cache unchanged. One additive JSON key. Next: (3) Test Mode difference report + Yes/No adoption.

## 0.9.4.135 — Test Mode difference report + Yes/No index adoption

User request (3): Test Mode re-analyzes everything, so it can reveal differences against the main index. On differences, report them and let the user choose Yes/No whether to update the main index -- explicit confirmation instead of automatic adoption (isolation contract preserved).
### Change
- Diff computation on Test Mode completion: compares main vs scratch -- changed (fingerprint/size mismatch), added (scratch only), removed (main only, inside the test scan scope and not ignored), pairDiff (symmetric pair-set difference). Cancelled scans are skipped; zero differences -> status "matches".
- GUI: non-modal Yes/No report (changed/new/removed/pairs A->B). No -> nothing changes.
- Adoption: APPLY_TEST_RESULT (additive command) -> backend worker thread, ONE transaction (ATTACH + DELETE/INSERT SELECT over files/matches/thumbs/content_hash/file_trace/meta) -- atomic, rolls back on failure/cancel (main index untouched), no file swap/WAL side effects. After adoption the thumbnail store/forget base point back at the main index and thumbnails are pruned.
### Verification
- backend_e2e Test 1d: preserved-mtime edit -> diff changed=1, pairDiff>=1 -> Yes -> testApplied ok and the main DB fingerprint actually changes (SQLite check). Test 1e: No -> fingerprint unchanged. Existing 1b/1c kept. Seven ui_settings keys. The first implementation used QDialog::open(), which forces window-modal and let the e2e modal-closer close the report; switched to show().
- CPU 125/125, GPU 126/126.
### Version
0.9.4.134 -> 0.9.4.135. Verdicts/storage/engine/DB/schema/cache/journal schema/kProtocol unchanged (additive command/events only). Limitations: adoption is wholesale for the test scan's scope; the JPEG thumbnail cache is keyed by (path,mtime,size), so size+mtime-preserving changes may keep an old thumbnail (pre-existing cache-key limitation).

## 0.9.4.136 — Preview-size gauge: 1.0 reference + drag ratio + list-view disabled

Field request for the right-pane preview-size gauge: (1) show the 1.0 (default 128 px) reference, (2) show the ratio while dragging (0.5/1.1/1.5), (3) gray and non-draggable in list view.
### Change
- `ZoomSlider` (QSlider subclass): light gray vertical line + triangular tick at the reference value (dimmer when disabled); a ratio bubble above the handle while dragging (one decimal, positioned from the style groove/handle metrics with clamping); minimum height 30.
- `setViewMode(i)`: `zoom_->setEnabled(i == 0)` -- list view uses Qt's disabled (gray) style; grid view re-enables it.
- Tooltip key `zoomTip` ("Preview size (1.0 = default)", refreshed on language change), objectName `zoomSlider`.
### Verification
- `ui_scroll_regression_test`: added grid-enabled / list-disabled assertions (pass); existing scroll/view-mode regressions hold.
- `ui_settings_test`: zoomTip key exists. CPU 125/125, GPU 126/126. Marker/bubble are painted elements pinned through enabled state/tooltip/view mode; the visual check is a user eyeball item.
### Version
0.9.4.135 -> 0.9.4.136. Display-only; verdicts/storage/protocol/engine/DB/schema/cache unchanged. The bubble shows during mouse dragging only (keyboard/wheel changes do not show it); the marker position is style-metric based (approximation where styles differ).

## 0.9.4.137 — Preview gauge 0.05-step snapping + two-decimal ratio bubble

Field feedback (0.9.4.136): (1) show two decimals in the bubble, (2) the preview size changes too finely between 0.9 and 1.0 (thirteen 1-px steps). The user suggested 0.1 units.
### Judgment
- 0.1 units (12.8 px) would make 0.9 -> 1.0 a single 13 px jump with only 17 stops overall -- too coarse. **0.05 units (6.4 px, 33 stops)** removes the "too many changes" problem while keeping the second decimal meaningful (0.95 -> 1.00 -> 1.05).
### Change
- `ZoomSlider::snapValueFor`: snaps to 0.05 x ratio via `round(round((v/128)/0.05)*0.05*128)` (0.40..2.00).
- `onValueChanged`: re-sets the value to the snap (QSignalBlocker prevents re-entry) and emits `previewSizeChanged(px)` with the **snapped value only**. MainWindow connects that signal to zoomChanged (the raw valueChanged is no longer used). singleStep 6 px / pageStep 26 px.
- Bubble: `round(ratio*100)/100` rendered with two decimals (0.50/0.95/1.00).
### Verification
- ui_scroll_regression assertions: 116 -> 115 px and 129 -> 128 px (1.0) snapping with the file-grid icon size following (both pass). The 0.9.4.136 assertions remain. CPU 125/125, GPU 126/126.
### Version
0.9.4.136 -> 0.9.4.137. Display-only. Snapping makes 51 px (0.40x) the effective minimum; internal `zoomChanged(px)` calls bypass snapping (contract kept).
